note: Friday 30 Oct 2026 07:02 SGT run, covering the Thursday 29 Oct US close / pre-Asia-open snapshot. S&P 500 -0.30% to 7720.39, Nasdaq -1.38% to 26184.72, Dow -0.25% to 52342.56, Russell 2000 +1.01% to 2859.22, VIX +1.72% to 17.20 -- a risk-off day driven by Alphabet's cash-flow miss even as Microsoft beat and small caps rallied. Equity Fear & Greed sits at 36 (Fear), roughly flat on the day but up from 20 a week ago; CNN's own site still blocks automated fetch (451/403) so the value is cross-checked across two third-party trackers that mirror its methodology. Crypto Fear & Greed at 51 (Neutral) as Bitcoin slid toward ,690. Breadth is narrow-at-the-top: short-term measures (50-DMA 61%, McClellan +21) look constructive but the 200-DMA participation picture (~56%) is only middling, and Thursday's index decline was concentrated in mega-cap AI names while the average stock held up better. Fund flows remain one week stale (week ended 2026-10-21, BofA/EPFR 'Enter the Dragon' report) -- the week-ended-28-Oct edition was not yet published/indexed as of this run; it would be the first to capture the FOMC decision and this week's Asia volatility.

flows.period: week ending 2026-10-21 (most recent published EPFR/Lipper weekly cut as of this run; the week-ending-Oct-28 release had not been published/indexed yet)
flows.narrative: Global equity funds extended their inflow streak to a fifth straight week, led by a sharp rotation into Asia/China (China funds' best week since July) and technology, even as a large chunk of capital still parked in money-market funds. Gold's 13-week inflow streak into physically-backed ETFs broke as bullion sold off into Oct 23, while bond buying continued steadily.

Broad 'gold funds' category still positive (BofA/EPFR), but Lipper showed physically-backed gold ETFs specifically saw a rare -$1.21B outflow in the week to Oct 23, ending a 13-week inflow streak, amid a ~4% bullion selloff.

movements.note: Consumer funds suffered their biggest outflow since Feb 2014 while tech pulled in its largest weekly haul since July -- a barbell rotation into AI/mega-cap exposure and away from consumer-discretionary risk.
China's $17B week (strongest since July) and broader EM's $33.5B dwarfed the more modest US (+$6.7B) and Europe (+$9.14B) inflows.
A large cash build coexisted with simultaneous aggressive buying of both equities and bonds -- consistent with BofA's framing that nobody is fully committed, everyone is still hedging.
First gold ETF outflow in 13 weeks as bullion fell ~4% that week, suggesting some profit-taking rotation out of the safe-haven trade.
